packets.title: Bake an expression to optimized keyframes
packets.responsibility: Converts a live expression into an optimized keyframe set via three Ramer-Douglas-Peucker passes: Pass A picks WHERE keys land (per-axis, unioned across axes), Pass B fits HOW each segment eases (verified against the exact evalCurvePoints evaluator that will render it, not a hand-ported copy), Pass C greedily merges adjacent Pass-A segments a single curve can still reconstruct within tolerance. A fully-constant expression collapses to zero keyframes (motionStatic only).
packets.writer: holder.motion[prop] (track replaced wholesale over [frameStart,frameEnd]); ex.enabled=false after baking
packets.public_api: window.SMExprBake = {bakeExpressionToKeyframes, _rdp, _fitSegmentCurve, _unionKeyframeTimes (exposed for unit tests only)}
consumers: a right-panel 'Bake' button (out of this census's bounded files)
packets.oracle: tests/expr-bake.test.cjs — dedicated test file, real coverage
packets.notes: Deliberately does not fit Position's spatial hOut/hIn bezier handles (a 2D point-cloud curve-fit, harder than the 1D progress-curve fit this file does) — a documented, intentional limitation, not a defect.

packets.responsibility: Shape-feature extraction (Fourier descriptors, similarity-transform fitting) and the Hungarian-algorithm bipartite matcher that pairs strokes between two keyframes for tweening. autoMatch tries a WASM path first with a silent JS fallback (autoMatchJS) per CLAUDE.md §3's documented 'a Rust-only bug can hide behind the JS fallback' pattern. relationalRefine/uncrossMatches post-process the raw assignment to fix crossed/tangled correspondences.
packets.writer: none (pure computation, returns a match plan)

packets.notes: CLAUDE.md §1 documents that brush-texture dabs are explicitly filtered out (splitTweenables) before this matcher runs — letting them in previously caused O(n^3) blowups and nonsensical cross-shape pairings.

packets.title: Feature-aware resampling and per-vertex warping
packets.responsibility: Resamples two strokes to a shared point count using feature-aware correspondence (landmark detection, dynamic-time-warping, moving-least-squares per-vertex fitting) rather than naive arc-length resampling — the machinery that makes a tween between two hand-drawn shapes with different vertex counts/starting points correspond visually, not just numerically.
packets.public_api: none (bare top-level functions)
consumers: C02.tween-engine.interpolation-core
packets.notes: The single densest, least-tested cluster in this census by line count (~850 lines, zero direct test references) — a strong candidate for a characterization test before any future refactor touches it.

The alignment helpers correct for closed-shape rotation/starting-point ambiguity before interpolating.

cross_cutting_notes: tweens.js (5278 lines, in scope apart from C01's undo/redo slice) has no window.SM*-style namespace export — unlike every other file in this census, and the codebase's general post-2026-07 convention, it declares dozens of bare top-level `function` names that become implicit globals, re-exposed piecemeal by timeline.js's own window.SM object (e.g. `generateTweens:generateTweens`). A future extraction of this file needs to either introduce a real namespace or explicitly enumerate its true public surface — 'everything is technically global' is not a real module boundary.

This census's file list overlaps two sibling census tasks in shared files, both verified directly against the sibling's own delivered JSON rather than assumed: tweens.js:4753-5022 (undo/redo/history) is owned by C01/#1036 (Fizz); timeline.js's bulk (renderTimeline/renderLayerList and most UI construction) is owned by C04a/C04b/C05/C06, and this census's timeline.js slice is limited to the six integration points listed in scope_files.

Three separate easing/curve implementations coexist by deliberate team decision, not accidental drift: animation/curve.js's evalCurvePoints (well-tested, extraction-ready), camera.js's own bezierEase (partially tested via cross-solver comparison against curve.js and text-selector.js), and ui.js's editor evaluator (out of this census's bounded files, explicitly documented by curve.js's own header comment as textually independent — 'this extraction changes no math'). Recorded here only so the orchestrator has the full picture in one place.

Every 'oracle: none found' claim in this census was produced by grepping the complete tests/ directory for both the file's basename and its exposed namespace/symbol names before being recorded — see coverage_note. This discipline was adopted directly after this session observed a sibling PR (#1080/#1081) where an unverified 'zero test coverage' claim was checked and found false by an independent reviewer.

The CLAUDE.md §5ter/§5quater engine-retention optimizations (retained paths, loadFrame reuse) key off identity/dirty-flag invariants on data this census's packets write (motion.js's transformSegments output, tweens.js's generateTweens-written frames). None of those optimizations' own invariant-check code lives inside this census's bounded files, but a future change to a C02 packet's writer semantics (e.g. replacing vs. mutating a track key in place) should be cross-checked against them before merging.

Fixing that catch-all exposed the SAME defect in the other seven motion-advanced packets: component-shape-tree, 3d-layers-and-gizmo, point-mapping-and-parent-chain, transform-application, duplicator-and-effector-props, geometry-motion-integrations and time-remap had all previously declared ONLY their export-table line(s) ('per export object lines …') — their real implementations were physically inside the old catch-all too. All seven now carry real ranges (this pass, grepped by exact symbol name against motion.js, not estimated).

Found but NOT corrected in this pass (out of scope — outside the motion-advanced area Pollen's #1084 review covered; needs its own follow-up using the same per-symbol-grep method): the identical declared-range-vs-real-location mismatch also affects at least three siblings elsewhere in motion.js. C02.properties-and-curves.keyframe-track-model's higher-level writers (valueAtFrame@2654, toggleAnimated@2764, setKeyAtCurrentFrame@2712, removeKeyAtCurrentFrame@2732, setValue@2820) sit nowhere near its declared 1178-1338, which only covers the lower-level ensureTrack/hasKeys/keyAt/rawValueAtFrame cluster. C02.properties-and-curves.key-selection-and-clipboard's declared 1033-1157 doesn't contain distributeKeys/flipKeys/selectEveryNthKey/invertKeySelection/applyMarqueeSelection/shiftKeySelection or keysLockedTo — their real implementation is the ease-curve/marquee/skew-drag engine at roughly motion.js:8553-8568 and 11427-13139. C02.expressions.expression-runtime's declared 1333-1783 ends well before evalExpressionFor/exprSelfAt/exprLayer/exprLayerControl/the alias-comp helpers, whose real implementation continues to roughly motion.js:2653. Also, C02.properties-and-curves.properties-and-metadata's declared 118-560 is short on the high end — its own PROP_LABEL/PROP_DIM/PROP_UNIT/PROP_DEFAULT/PROP_DIM_LABELS tables and several of its own listed symbols continue to at least motion.js:899, with C02.motion-advanced.duplicator-and-effector-props's DUP_TARGET_PROPS/DUP_OFFSET_PROP constants (motion.js:581-582) embedded inside that extended block. A programmatic pairwise-overlap check (run as part of this correction) confirms these three siblings' OWN declared ranges also overlap each other pre-existing, independent of the catch-all: curves-and-easing's 941-1177 fully contains key-selection-and-clipboard's declared 1033-1157, and keyframe-track-model's declared 1178-1338 overlaps expression-runtime's declared 1333-1783 by six lines (1333-1338). Neither was introduced by this pass — both were already present in the reviewed #1084 candidate. The same check found zero new overlaps among this pass's corrected motion-advanced ranges, and zero overlap between them and any of the five sibling ranges Pollen's review named; the only other overlaps it found are between different packets' own export-table line CITATIONS (e.g. transform-application's and geometry-motion-integrations's, or 3d-layers-and-gizmo's and duplicator's) — expected, since window.SMMotion's single export object literal interleaves many packets' key:value lines within the same numeric span, and citing that span coarsely (as every packet in this census already does) will always look like it 'overlaps' a neighbor's export citation without being a real implementation double-claim.
